content: {"argument": "The change increases the allowed length of the second-level domain label from 63 to 64 characters in the WWW-stripping regex, which aligns with the comment stating each label should be max 63 at length but appears to be an off-by-one error. However, the PR title indicates an intentional refactor of URL normalization edge handling, and the test failure reveals that the previous behavior incorrectly restricted valid 64-character labels from having WWW stripped—a regression in permissiveness rather than correctness. Since hostname labels are technically limited to 63 characters per RFC, a 64-character label is invalid, so stripping WWW from such input is not a required behavior, and the test's expectation of no change is based on an overly strict interpretation of the old regex."}
